sections.title: باب 3 — متن (152)

paras.text: … preserved. In the beginning, whatever the noble Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) heard, learned or saw from the Noble Prophet ﷺ, they would preserve it in their minds, in practical form and in written form, but there was no regular book. At the end of the Umayyad era and the beginning of the Abbasid era, the tendency to compile collections of ahadith gained strength, and many collections of ahadith were compiled. But along with this, some short-sighted people, for the support of their political and religious views, also began to spread wrong and forged ahadith among them, because of which non-authentic and weak ahadith too got included along with authentic ones in the collection of ahadith. Now the need arose that authentic and sahih ahadith be sifted out from non-authentic and weak ahadith and separated, and collections of purely sahih ahadith be compiled. So in the third century Hijri the great muhaddithin accomplished this work and compiled six books of sahih ahadith, which are called the Sihah Sittah (the six authentic books). They are as follows:

… preserved. In the beginning, whatever the noble Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) heard, learned or saw from the Noble Prophet ﷺ, they would preserve it in their minds, in practical form and in written form, but there was no regular book. At the end of the Umayyad era and the beginning of the Abbasid era, the tendency to compile collections of ahadith gained strength, and many collections of ahadith were compiled. But along with this, some short-sighted people, for the support of their political and religious views, also began to spread wrong and forged ahadith among them, because of which non-authentic and weak ahadith too got included along with authentic ones in the collection of ahadith. Now the need arose that authentic and sahih ahadith be sifted out from non-authentic and weak ahadith and separated, and collections of purely sahih ahadith be compiled. So in the third century Hijri the great muhaddithin accomplished this work and compiled six books of sahih ahadith, which are called the Sihah Sittah (the six authentic books). They are as follows:

1. Sahih Bukhari, compiled by Imam Muhammad bin Isma'il Bukhari (may Allah have mercy on him)

2. Sahih Muslim, compiled by Imam Muslim bin Hajjaj Nishapuri (may Allah have mercy on him)

3. Sunan Ibn Majah, by Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid Qazwini (may Allah have mercy on him)

4. Sunan Abu Dawud, by Abu Dawud Sulayman bin al-Ash'ath Sijistani (may Allah have mercy on him)

5. Jami' Tirmidhi, compiled by Abu Muhammad bin 'Isa Tirmidhi (may Allah have mercy on him)

6. Sunan Nasa'i, compiled by Abu Abd al-Rahman Ahmad bin Shu'ayb bin Ali al-Nasa'i (may Allah have mercy on him)

Besides the Sihah Sittah, the following books of Hadith too hold a prominent position.

1. Muwatta', by Imam Malik

2. Kitab al-Zuhd wa al-Raqa'iq, by Imam Abdullah bin Mubarak (may Allah have mercy on him)

3. Kitab al-Kharaj, by Imam Abu Yusuf (may Allah have mercy on him)

4. Musnad Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, by Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on him), etc.

sections.title: باب 3 — متن (153)

paras.text: … those narrators through whom the hadith reaches us are called the sanad.
paras.urdu: راویوں جن کے ذریعے حدیث ہم تک پہنچتی ہے کو سند کہتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: … چې د هغوی له لارې حدیث موږ ته رسېږي، سند وايي.

paras.text: When at the end of the Banu Umayyah and the beginning of the caliphate of the Banu Abbas the ahadith were collected, then this science began. In a branch of this science, "Asma' al-Rijal", the life-circumstances of more than five hundred thousand people were collected, and through it this became known: which narrator is reliable, and which ahadith are sahih, which hasan, which da'if and which rejected.
paras.urdu: بنو امیہ کے آخر اور بنو عباس کے دورِ خلافت کے شروع میں احادیث جمع کی گئیں تب اس علم کا آغاز ہوا۔ اس علم کی ایک شاخ ”اسماء الرجال“ میں پانچ لاکھ سے زیادہ لوگوں کے حالاتِ زندگی کو جمع کیا گیا اور اس کے ذریعے یہ معلوم ہوا کہ کون سا راوی قابلِ اعتبار ہے اور کون سی احادیث صحیح ہیں، کون سی حسن، کون سی ضعیف اور کون سی مردود۔
paras.pashto: کله چې د بنو امیه په پای او د بنو عباس د خلافت په پیل کې احادیث راټول شول، نو د دې علم پیل وشو. د دې علم په یوه څانګه «اسماء الرجال» کې له پنځه لکه زیاتو خلکو د ژوند حالات راټول شول، او د هغې له لارې معلومه شوه چې کوم راوي د باور وړ دی، او کوم احادیث صحیح، کوم حسن، کوم ضعیف او کوم مردود دي.

paras.text: v. The science of fiqh
paras.urdu: v۔ علمِ فقہ
paras.pashto: v. د فقه علم

paras.text: The verbal meaning of fiqh is "to know something", to make clear and open the real meaning of something. In Shari'ah terminology, the knowledge of the issues of Shari'ah deeds is called "fiqh". Among these issues, issues of every kind of worship and dealings are included. The science of fiqh has four basic sources: the Quran, the Sunnah, qiyas (analogy) and ijma' (consensus). The regular beginning of the science of fiqh started in the era of Hazrat Amir Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him) in 41 Hijri. In this era Hadith was being compiled (mudawwan), therefore a distinction was made between hadith and opinion, and the regular science of fiqh began. As a result of it four great schools of fiqh were formed. The first of them is Imam Abu Hanifah (may Allah have mercy on him). His school attained the greatest fame. It is called the Hanafi school. The second is Imam Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), whose school is called Shafi'i; the third is Imam Malik (may Allah have mercy on him), who was in the Hijaz; they are called Maliki; and the fourth is Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on him), whose school is called Hanbali. All these noble jurists made the laws of the Islamic Shari'ah clear in book form. All are authentic and reliable and exactly in accordance with the Shari'ah. … those narrators through whom the hadith reaches us are called the sanad.

When at the end of the Banu Umayyah and the beginning of the caliphate of the Banu Abbas the ahadith were collected, then this science began. In a branch of this science, "Asma' al-Rijal", the life-circumstances of more than five hundred thousand people were collected, and through it this became known: which narrator is reliable, and which ahadith are sahih, which hasan, which da'if and which rejected.

v. The science of fiqh

The verbal meaning of fiqh is "to know something", to make clear and open the real meaning of something. In Shari'ah terminology, the knowledge of the issues of Shari'ah deeds is called "fiqh". Among these issues, issues of every kind of worship and dealings are included. The science of fiqh has four basic sources: the Quran, the Sunnah, qiyas (analogy) and ijma' (consensus). The regular beginning of the science of fiqh started in the era of Hazrat Amir Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him) in 41 Hijri. In this era Hadith was being compiled (mudawwan), therefore a distinction was made between hadith and opinion, and the regular science of fiqh began. As a result of it four great schools of fiqh were formed. The first of them is Imam Abu Hanifah (may Allah have mercy on him). His school attained the greatest fame. It is called the Hanafi school. The second is Imam Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), whose school is called Shafi'i; the third is Imam Malik (may Allah have mercy on him), who was in the Hijaz; they are called Maliki; and the fourth is Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on him), whose school is called Hanbali. All these noble jurists made the laws of the Islamic Shari'ah clear in book form. All are authentic and reliable and exactly in accordance with the Shari'ah. فقہ کا لفظی معنی ہے ”کسی چیز کو جاننا“، کسی شئے کے حقیقی معنی واضح کرنا اور کھولنا“۔ شرعی اصطلاح میں اعمالِ شرعیہ کے مسائل کا علم ”فقہ“ کہلاتا ہے۔ ان مسائل میں عبادات اور معاملات تمام طرح کے مسائل شامل ہیں۔ علمِ فقہ کے چار بنیادی ماخذ ہیں۔ قرآن، سنت، قیاس اور اجماع۔ علمِ فقہ کا باقاعدہ آغاز حضرت امیر معاویہ رضی اللہ عنہ کے دور میں 41 ہجری سے شروع ہوا۔ اس دور میں حدیث کو مُدَوَّن کیا جا رہا تھا اس لیے حدیث اور رائے میں فرق کیا گیا اور باقاعدہ علمِ فقہ کا آغاز ہوا۔ جس کے نتیجے میں چار بڑے فقہی مذاہب بنے۔ جن میں پہلے امام ابو حنیفہ رحمۃ اللہ علیہ ہیں۔ ان کے مسلک کو سب سے زیادہ شہرت حاصل ہوئی۔ اسے حنفی مذہب کہا جاتا ہے۔ دوسرے امام شافعی رحمۃ اللہ علیہ جن کے مذہب کو شافعی اور تیسرے امام مالک رحمۃ اللہ علیہ جو حجاز میں تھے۔ ان کو مالکی کہا جاتا ہے اور چوتھے امام احمد بن حنبل رحمۃ اللہ علیہ جن کا مذہب حنبلی کہلاتا ہے۔ ان تمام فقہائے کرام نے شریعتِ اسلامی کے قوانین کو کتابی شکل میں واضح کیا۔ سب مستند اور قابلِ اعتبار ہیں اور شریعت کے عین مطابق ہیں۔ ہر دور میں مختلف علاقوں کے لوگ ان کے پیروکار ہیں۔ سب سے زیادہ لوگ فقہ حنفی کو ماننے والے ہیں۔

vi۔ اصولِ فقہ

علمِ اصولِ فقہ شرعی مسائل کے دلائل سے بحث کرتا ہے۔ اس علم میں بھی دورِ عباسیہ میں خوب ترقی ہوئی اور بے شمار کتب تحریر کی گئیں اور نہایت کامیابی کے ساتھ اس علم کو مدون کیا گیا۔ جو بعد میں آنے والے لوگوں کے لیے رہنمائی فراہم کرتا ہے۔ اصولِ فقہ پر ایک مستند کتاب امام شافعی رحمۃ اللہ علیہ کی ”الرسالۃ فی علم الاصول“ ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ امام محمد رحمۃ اللہ اور امام ابو یوسف رحمۃ اللہ وغیرہ کی کتب قابلِ ذکر ہیں۔

… those narrators through whom the hadith reaches us are called the sanad.

When at the end of the Banu Umayyah and the beginning of the caliphate of the Banu Abbas the ahadith were collected, then this science began. In a branch of this science, "Asma' al-Rijal", the life-circumstances of more than five hundred thousand people were collected, and through it this became known: which narrator is reliable, and which ahadith are sahih, which hasan, which da'if and which rejected.

v. The science of fiqh

The verbal meaning of fiqh is "to know something", to make clear and open the real meaning of something. In Shari'ah terminology, the knowledge of the issues of Shari'ah deeds is called "fiqh". Among these issues, issues of every kind of worship and dealings are included. The science of fiqh has four basic sources: the Quran, the Sunnah, qiyas (analogy) and ijma' (consensus). The regular beginning of the science of fiqh started in the era of Hazrat Amir Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him) in 41 Hijri. In this era Hadith was being compiled (mudawwan), therefore a distinction was made between hadith and opinion, and the regular science of fiqh began. As a result of it four great schools of fiqh were formed. The first of them is Imam Abu Hanifah (may Allah have mercy on him). His school attained the greatest fame. It is called the Hanafi school. The second is Imam Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), whose school is called Shafi'i; the third is Imam Malik (may Allah have mercy on him), who was in the Hijaz; they are called Maliki; and the fourth is Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on him), whose school is called Hanbali. All these noble jurists made the laws of the Islamic Shari'ah clear in book form. All are authentic and reliable and exactly in accordance with the Shari'ah. In every era people of various regions are their followers. The largest number of people are followers of Hanafi fiqh.

vi. Principles of fiqh (Usul al-Fiqh)

The science of usul al-fiqh discusses the proofs of Shari'ah issues. In this science too, great progress took place in the Abbasid era, and countless books were written, and with great success this science was compiled. It provides guidance for those who came later. An authoritative book on usul al-fiqh is "al-Risalah fi 'Ilm al-Usul" of Imam Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him). Besides this, the books of Imam Muhammad (may Allah have mercy on him) and Imam Abu Yusuf (may Allah have mercy on him) etc. are worth mentioning.

vii. Tasawwuf (Sufism)

In different eras some change has been found in the meaning and sense of tasawwuf. But on this matter all agree that tasawwuf is in fact the name of the purity of the heart and the purification of the soul. The real Sufi is only he who at all times [keeps] his bond with Allah, the Lord of Honour …
